text:
sophia: Hey team — prepping a small docs PR to clarify how to set the geo header to prefer EU endpoints for customers who want data locality. Can someone confirm the SDK snippet for Node and Go? I want to include curl + SDK usage and a short note about fallback behaviour.

alex: Quick note — legal asked us to avoid the phrase \"data residency\" in the public guide unless it's contract-backed. Use \"data routing preference\" or similar. @legal can confirm.

maria: I can run the snippets today. Do we have the canonical header name? Was it `X-Redwood-Region` or `X-Region`? I remember infra changed it recently.

kevin: infra changed it to `x-redwood-region` (lowercase is canonical in our SDKs) last month. Older examples still use `X-Region` — we should document both and say the kebab-case header is preferred.

docs-bot: deploy preview available: https://deploy.example.com/preview/789 (build #452) :white_check_mark:

maria: Tested Node snippet — small fix needed: when using fetch in Node, headers get normalized so use lowercase key or Headers constructor. Working example I used:```js
// Node fetch example
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'authorization': 'Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY',
    'content-type': 'application/json',
    'x-redwood-region': 'eu-west-1' // preferred header
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hello' })
});
```

sophia: Nice. Can we add a one-line caveat that private deployments might ignore this header (customer-controlled routing)? Also include a link to the endpoints matrix.

legal: Please change any public wording from \"guarantees\" or \"residency\" to \"routing preference\". Add this sentence near the top: \"Setting a region header expresses a routing preference; guaranteed data residency is only provided under specific contractual agreements.\" I can approve the exact phrasing in the PR.

alex: I'll add legal's sentence. Also suggest we show what happens on fallback: when the requested region isn't available we route to the nearest compatible shard and attach a response header `x-redwood-routed-region`. Add a short troubleshooting step to check request routing with the CLI: `rwctl routes show <request-id>` (internal).

kevin: Infra ops confirms `x-redwood-routed-region` is emitted on routed requests. Also log search tip: `service:gateway region:eu*` helps find failed routing. Add that to the troubleshooting section.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4323 — includes Node + Go snippets, legal wording, and the fallback note. Deploy preview link above updated.

sophia: Follow-up: can someone polish the Go SDK snippet to show context timeout and header injection? Proposed snippet:```go
// Go example (context + header)
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
reqBody := map[string]interface{}{"prompt": "hello"}
reqBytes, _ := json.Marshal(reqBody)
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewReader(reqBytes))
req.Header.Set("authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
req.Header.Set("content-type", "application/json")
req.Header.Set("x-redwood-region", "eu-west-1") // routing preference
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
// handle resp / err
```

alex: pushed an update that includes the Go snippet and lowercase header examples. Also added a short note: \"If you need contractual data residency, contact sales/enterprise\" with the enterprise contact link.

docs-bot: @sophia requested review on PR #4323 — reviewers: @alex, @maria, @legal.

sophia: Thanks everyone — I think this covers it. After legal sign-off I'll merge and request a docs sweep to update any legacy pages still referencing `X-Region`. :thumbsup:
